newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian soymeal prices ease on dull export demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian soymeal prices ease on dull export demand.

text.p: Indian soymeal export prices eased by about $6-7 per tonne during the week due to dull demand, traders said on Tuesday.
They said soymeal for export was quoted at $320-$322 per tonne FAS compared with $327-$328 last week. Soymeal was quoted at about $272 per tonne this time last year.
Traders said they were not able to ship soymeal committed earlier for export due to poor availability. A rise in domestic consumption and fall in output had reduced availability for exports.

Traders said about 2.2 million tonnes of soymeal had been contracted for export in the 1996/97 (November-October) season compared with 2.6 million tonnes the previous season. Export demand was mainly from China, South Korea and the Middle East.
Soybean prices eased by about 600 to 700 rupees per tonne during the week due to a slight increase in domestic arrivals, traders said. Soybean was quoted at 12,800 to 13,200 rupees per tonne.
Arrivals were around 1,200 tonnes per day in the central Indian markets, the hub of India's soybean industry. --New Delhi newsroom +91-11 301 2024
